title: Emerald Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Emerald Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered scope, timeline, security/compliance needs (SOC2, KMS), network architecture (VPC/peering), deployment options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), initial pilot success criteria, and next steps for pilot setup and benchmarks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Ava Moreno (Redwood Onboarding), Dr. Karen Miles (Emerald Head of AI), Tony Ramirez (VP Eng), Maya Chen (DevOps), Liam O'Connor (Security), Renee Park (PM)

Summary (auto): Kickoff covering onboarding steps, security requirements, pilot scope and timeline. Agreed to run a 2-week dedicated capacity pilot and share artifacts.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Samir and Ava from our team, super excited to get started with Emerald Health, quick round robin, can folks say name and role?
[00:12] Dr. Karen Miles: Karen Miles, Head of AI at Emerald, I'll be owning the project from our side.
[00:17] Tony Ramirez: Tony, VP Engineering. We'll do infra and delivery.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Maya, DevOps, I'll be implementing the network side.
[00:24] Liam O'Connor: Liam, security.
[00:26] Renee Park: Renee, product manager for the pilot.
[00:29] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: scope, security/compliance, infra requirements, pilot success criteria, timelines, and action items. Anything to add?
[00:38] Tony Ramirez: No, that covers it. We're mainly interested in two things: latency for real-time triage and cost predictability.
[00:45] Samir Gupta: Yep, understood. Historically teams ask about hosted API first then Dedicated vs Private for PII workloads, seems like you might need Private or Dedicated?
[00:54] Dr. Karen Miles: We have PHI in clinical notes, so we need data controls. We prefer VPC/private deployment or dedicated capacity with our own KMS.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: That makes sense. Redwood Private would be the cleanest for full control; Dedicated gives isolation and can integrate with customer KMS in many cases. We'll walk through the tradeoffs.
[01:15] Ava Moreno: Practically for onboarding, we can spin up a Dedicated pool for a pilot within your cloud account or provision a Private instance depending on your compliance needs. For the pilot we usually recommend Dedicated for faster time-to-value.
[01:30] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we need to know what networking we need, do you support VPC peering or Transit Gateway?
[01:36] Samir Gupta: We support VPC peering and AWS Transit Gateway; for Private on-prem installs we'll need a network runbook, but for cloud Dedicated we can peer into your VPC and you can manage the security groups. We'll send the exact CIDR and port list.
[01:48] Liam O'Connor: Encryption at rest — do you integrate with customer KMS / HSM? We need to meet our internal encryption rules and SOC2 scope.
[01:56] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated in most deployments. For hosted we use Redwood-managed keys but can discuss bring-your-own-KMS options for enterprise tiers. We'll include SOC2 docs and our security whitepaper.
[02:08] Dr. Karen Miles: Great, please send the SOC2 report and any pen test summaries.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: Will do.
[02:14] Renee Park: On success criteria, we want sub-200ms p95 for the triage endpoint with a throughput of ~250 reqs/min, and cost below $X per 1k tokens, but we need realistic numbers.
[02:26] Samir Gupta: We'll baseline that in the perf run. For p95 under 200ms we often recommend model selection + quantization and batching configs; Dedicated with GPU pooling will be easiest to hit that. We'll provide a benchmark script you can run with sample payloads.
[02:41] Tony Ramirez: Does Redwood provide token-level cost breakdowns? That'd help us forecast.
[02:45] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. We'll set up a demo of the console as part of onboarding.
[02:54] Maya Chen: For network, aside from peering, do you need outbound NAT? Anything special for KV cache / persistent storage?
[03:00] Samir Gupta: The runtime keeps KV cache in memory across GPU workers, no persistent DB required for that, but for model artifacts we pull from an object store. We'll document S3/R2 endpoints and roles.
[03:12] Dr. Karen Miles: Our legal team will ask about data retention. For the pilot we need to ensure logs with PHI are not persisted beyond X days.
[03:20] Jordan Lee: We support configurable retention policies and audit log export. We'll map retention to your requirements, and we can disable request logging for sensitive routes if needed.
[03:30] Renee Park: Timeline — we'd like to start a pilot in early December, run two weeks, then evaluate. Is that realistic?
[03:36] Jordan Lee: Yes, that aligns. We'll aim to have the Dedicated pool and benchmark scripts ready within 4-6 business days after we get the network info.
[03:44] Tony Ramirez: What will we need from infra to get started?
[03:47] Ava Moreno: Network CIDR, IAM role for S3 access for model artifacts, KMS key ARN if you're using customer-managed keys, and a small test dataset for benchmarking.
[03:56] Maya Chen: I'll put together the CIDR and the role. We might need a short maintenance window to add peering.
[04:02] Liam O'Connor: Also, we'll need the contact for your compliance person for SOC2/attestations.
[04:07] Jordan Lee: I'll include our security lead's contact in the docs we send.
[04:10] Samir Gupta: Quick note on models: for triage we often recommend a smaller, optimized seq2seq model or a chat-moderated pipeline to reduce latency. For clinical summarization we recommend a higher-capacity model, but we can test both during pilot.
[04:25] Dr. Karen Miles: We're interested in both triage and summarization; triage is priority.
[04:29] Renee Park: Success metrics: p95 latency, classification accuracy on N labeled cases above 92%, and no PII leakage in logs. We'll formalize that doc and send it.
[04:39] Jordan Lee: Perfect. On the pilot we'll instrument quality checks and tie them to our Redwood Optimize alerts so we can watch regressions.
[04:47] Tony Ramirez: Cost — can we get an estimate for the 2-week pilot and then for steady state?
[04:52] Jordan Lee: We'll provide a cost projection based on your expected throughput and token usage; for the pilot we'll give a capped estimate. Samir will share the benchmarking template to estimate cost.
[05:02] Samir Gupta: I'll drop the template and example numbers. Also, there are a couple of caveats: if you need model quantization to save cost, we'll propose a compatibility matrix.
[05:12] Dr. Karen Miles: Any dependencies on our side for model fine-tuning? We do want to iterate on prompts first.
[05:18] Samir Gupta: Prompts are straightforward; for finetune or RLHF style workflows we can recommend a workflow but for pilot we recommend prompt engineering and maybe light instruction tuning.
[05:28] Jordan Lee: Let's go through an example timeline: Today kickoff, Jordan sends deck + next steps by Friday, Maya sends network details by Tuesday, we spin up Dedicated pilot by Dec 1, run perf & quality tests for two weeks, then joint review in mid-December.
[05:44] Renee Park: Works for our calendar.
[05:46] Liam O'Connor: Quick security question — do you offer SAML/SSO for RBAC to the console?
[05:51] Jordan Lee: Yes, enterprise bundles include SSO via SAML and role-based access; we'll include setup steps.
[05:57] Maya Chen: Are there log forwarding options? SIEM integrations?
[06:00] Samir Gupta: Yes, we support CloudWatch, Datadog, and generic syslog forwarding for audit logs.
[06:06] Dr. Karen Miles: On model catalog, can we pin a model version to avoid regressions?
[06:10] Jordan Lee: Absolutely, pinning and rollouts (canary/A-B) are built into Redwood Console. We'll show that in the demo.
[06:17] Tony Ramirez: Who do we talk to about contractual terms for Dedicated capacity?
[06:21] Jordan Lee: I'll loop in Sales and Legal; initial pilot typically runs under a short-term usage agreement and then we discuss reserved capacity commits if you want steady-state predictable pricing.
[06:33] Renee Park: Any recommended sample sizes for the quality eval?
[06:36] Samir Gupta: For classification triage, 500 labeled examples is a good start to get statistically meaningful precision/recall. For summarization, 100-200 prompt/eval pairs to start.
[06:47] Dr. Karen Miles: We'll start collection this week.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: Ok let's recap and action items. We'll send onboarding deck, security docs (SOC2), benchmark script, and the Dedicated pilot plan. Customer to send network diagram, KMS info, and success criteria doc.
[07:04] Tony Ramirez: Sounds good. Is there a follow-up tech deep dive penciled in?
[07:08] Jordan Lee: We suggested a technical deep dive with Samir and your infra team next week — propose Dec 1 or Dec 2?
[07:15] Maya Chen: Dec 2 works better for us.
[07:17] Jordan Lee: Great, we'll schedule Dec 2 for the technical deep dive.
[07:21] Renee Park: One last ask — can you share a sample runbook for incidents and escalation matrix?
[07:25] Ava Moreno: Yes, we'll include our standard runbook template and a proposed escalation path.
[07:29] Dr. Karen Miles: Thank you, excited to get started.
[07:31] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
[07:35] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains automatic speaker labels and some minor transcription errors (names and acronyms occasionally garbled).
